item.title: The Moscow Times: Putin Orders Private Data Centers to Set Aside 10% of Capacity to Support IT Infrastructure
item.description: Russian data centers have become targets of Ukrainian drone attacks in recent weeks.

item.title: The Moscow Times: Russia Officially Withdraws From Europe’s Anti-Torture Convention
item.description: Russia ratified the anti-torture treaty in 1998, two years after joining the Council of Europe. It announced its decision to withdraw in October 2025.

item.title: The Moscow Times: Russian Discount Retailer Fix Price Exits Mongolia
item.description: Industry analysts said Mongolia’s small market size and logistical challenges in the country likely made it difficult for Fix Price to run a sustainable business there.

item.title: The Moscow Times: FSB Claims Ukraine Sent Drone Goggles Rigged With Explosives to Russian Volunteers
item.description: The devices were allegedly wired to detonate immediately upon being turned on, killing or injuring the operators, the FSB said.

item.title: The Moscow Times: Oleshky Ceasefire and Aid Operation End Without Any Violations, Lantratova Says
item.description: The Kremlin called the humanitarian operation a success, praising the “level of coordination achieved among participants from all sides.”

item.title: The Moscow Times: Kremlin Downplays Prospect of Resuming Gas Shipments to Europe via Ukraine
item.description: U.S. officials reportedly suggested the idea during talks in September as an incentive for Russia to halt strikes on Ukraine’s energy grid.

item.title: The Moscow Times: Ukrainian Drones Hit Major Oil Transport Hub in Samara Region
item.description: The Transneft-owned facility, which moves crude toward refineries and pipelines in western Russia, has been repeatedly attacked this month.

item.title: The Moscow Times: FSB Arrests Minor Over Moscow Park Attack Threat After U.S. Tip-Off
item.description: The U.S. Embassy in Moscow had issued an urgent security alert warning of a credible threat of a mass casualty event.

item.title: The Moscow Times: Cyberattack Hits Rosstat as Hackers Claim Huge Data Theft
item.description: Hackers claimed to have stolen 23 terabytes of data, including information on Russian losses in the war in Ukraine.

item.title: The Moscow Times: Russia’s Independent Journalism Will Survive in Exile, Gershkovich Says at Inaugural Derk Sauer Lecture
item.description: The event was both a tribute to Sauer’s legacy and a discussion of Gershkovich’s work and imprisonment in Russia.

item.title: The Moscow Times: U.S. Embassy Warns of Potential 'Mass Casualty Event' in Moscow
item.description: Russia's FSB said it had received the report and was "taking appropriate action."

item.title: The Moscow Times: Oleshky Evacuees Arrive in Ukraine
item.description: To reach Ukrainian-held territory, residents had to take a complicated route via occupied Crimea, Anapa and Belarus.

item.title: The Moscow Times: Japan Demands Release of Detained Journalist at G20 Meeting
item.description: The case adds to long-running tensions between Russia and Japan.

item.title: The Moscow Times: At the Third Russia-Africa Summit, Moscow Talked Big. But Who Was Listening?
item.description: The picture of how the Ukraine war is reverberating across Africa is much clearer than it was in 2023 — and it doesn’t look reassuring for Moscow.

item.title: The Moscow Times: Russia Designates Opposition Delegation at PACE as ‘Undesirable’
item.description: The delegation of Russian exiles was set up earlier this year to represent the anti-Kremlin opposition at Europe’s leading human rights body.

item.title: The Moscow Times: ‘The Right to Be Named’: Russians in Amsterdam Remember Victims of Political Repression
item.description: Established to remember people killed during Stalin’s Great Terror, Remembering the Names has since become an occasion to reflect on the relationship between Soviet violence and political repression in present-day Russia.

item.title: The Moscow Times: 3 Killed as Ukraine Renews Drone Strikes Against Oil Refineries
item.description: Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak confirmed that Ukrainian drones targeted three oil refineries and one gas chemical complex overnight.

item.title: The Moscow Times: Ex-Communist Party Lawmaker in Murmansk Accused of Passing Sensitive Information to Ukraine
item.description: Police arrested 76-year-old Gennady Stepakhno on Oct. 9, after which a judge ruled that he be placed in pre-trial detention for two months.

item.title: The Moscow Times: International Sports Court Overturns Ban on Russian Ice Hockey Teams
item.description: The International Ice Hockey Federation had banned Russia and Belarus from its competitions in response to the 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

item.title: The Moscow Times: Russia’s Oldest Independent Newspaper, Novaya Gazeta, Announces Closure
item.description: After more than 30 years in operation, the newspaper said it could no longer function amid mounting pressure from law enforcement authorities.

item.title: The Moscow Times: Aid Deliveries and Evacuations in Oleshky Begin After Demining Operation Wraps Up
item.description: Ukrainian and Russian officials said a humanitarian convoy is ready to depart for the besieged town in occupied southern Ukraine.

item.title: The Moscow Times: Russia to Extend Diesel Export Ban, Use Quotas to Fulfill U.S. Deal, Sources Say
item.description: The current ban on diesel exports is due to expire on Oct. 31.

item.title: The Moscow Times: State Duma Passes Record Defense Spending Budget in First Reading
item.description: The proposed record defense spending comes alongside a new wave of tax hikes designed to fund the rising costs of the war in Ukraine.

item.title: The Moscow Times: Moscow Judge Sentences Exiled Libertarian Mikhail Svetov to One Year in Prison
item.description: Svetov, who left Russia in 2021, was found guilty in absentia of violating the country’s “foreign agent” law.
